title: Weekly service
hook: one act for others each week
tomorrow: Ananda said good friends are half the path. what did the Buddha say?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: rest day, remembered and kept, a day when everyone under the roof rests. Today the week gets one more piece: something done for others.

Volunteer sign-up sheets usually start with the jobs: setup, serving, cleanup. At the Sikh Guru's town of Goindwal, the sign-up started somewhere else: on the floor, with a plate. Sikh tradition tells that when the Mughal emperor Akbar came to meet Guru Amar Das, the third Guru, he was given the rule: first the pangat, then the sangat. First sit in the row and eat, then come sit with the Guru. And the emperor sat down on the floor, in the row, with everyone else.
screen: `SETUP, SERVING, CLEANUP.` → `AN EMPEROR COMES TO GOINDWAL.` → `FIRST THE ROW, THEN THE GURU.` → `HE SITS ON THE FLOOR.`

segments.voice: The row is the langar, the Guru's free kitchen. Anyone may come, of any caste or religion, rich or poor, and everyone sits on the floor at the same level and eats the same simple food, dal and roti. The Guru Granth Sahib itself remembers a langar: it praises Mata Khivi, wife of the second Guru, giving out kheer, rice pudding, rich with ghee, sweet as nectar. Stand in that kitchen for a minute. The smell of ghee and onions. Flat breads coming off a hot griddle. Steel plates clinking down the row. Behind it all, someone up to their elbows in hot water and soap, scrubbing the pots. That someone is doing seva, selfless service, and for Sikhs it is a form of worship. Cooking, serving, washing, done for the Guru, for anyone at all, expecting nothing back. Now the order. You don't start by serving. You start by being served, sitting in the same row as everyone you'll serve. No one is above the row, not even an emperor. That is the teaching under weekly service: one act for others, done regularly, from the floor, at the same level as the people you serve.
screen: `THE LANGAR: ONE ROW, ONE FOOD.` · `MATA KHIVI'S KHEER AND GHEE.` · `SEVA: SERVICE AS WORSHIP.` · `SERVED FIRST, THEN SERVING.` · then, large: `ONE A WEEK.`

segments.voice: If there's a dish nearby, wash it by hand, slowly: the warm water, the soap, the weight of it, as if it were someone else's plate. If not, sit on the floor and rest your open hands on your knees. Then name one act you could do for others, once a week.
Weekly service: one act for others each week, done the langar way, at the same level as the people you serve, expecting nothing back.
The line for today: one a week, from the floor of the same row. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Gurdwaras run the langar, a free kitchen where volunteers cook, serve and wash up as seva, and everyone, Sikh or not, sits on the floor in rows and eats the same meal.
